correctness.rationale: The explicit density \(f(\xi)=1+0.3(\xi_3^2-1/3)\) is smooth, even, positive and nonconstant. The checked fiber formula has positive strong-convexity margin. More fundamentally, the Crofton construction for a smooth positive measure on the projective-line path geometry gives a reversible projective Finsler metric, and the Crofton length of any projective line is the total measure of the dual projective plane because two distinct projective lines meet once; hence all prime projective lines have the same length while the density need not be constant. The numerical Holmes–Thompson estimate is not used.

originality.rationale: Álvarez Paiva–Berck's general prescribed-geodesics Crofton theorem already constructs a Finsler metric from every smooth positive measure on a two-dimensional path geometry and identifies the prescribed curves as its geodesics. Applying it to projective lines on \(\mathbb{RP}^2\), the one-intersection incidence count immediately makes every line have the same Crofton length for every such measure. The record's nonconstant harmonic density is therefore a direct specialization of broader prior machinery, not a new counterexample principle.
